why: R11's `environment` signal asks whether our kernel declares anything about
a candidate held-out family's subject operators. It cannot be a threshold,
and measuring it is what shows why: `natural-square-root` is a legitimate
standing held-out family and we declare `Nat.sqrt`, `Nat.sqrt_zero` and
`Nat.sqrt_one` (draw 8 compared all four by hand; none is a mirror), while
a `natural-nth-root` candidate picks up 9 hits on the stem `root` whose top
is `Complex.root_of_unity_pow` -- unrelated mathematics sharing a word. No
count separates those. A person reading five names does, in a minute.
So a NEW held-out family whose sweep is non-empty must be reviewed here
before it may be drawn. The review must reproduce the LIVE sweep exactly:
that is what makes it a disclosure rather than a rubber stamp, because a
later declaration landing in that namespace changes the sweep and
invalidates the review instead of passing silently.
The DEMAND is scoped to draw time. Every standing held-out family was
preregistered before this screen existed, so demanding a review for one
retroactively would mean either a red gate on `main` or a file asserting
diligence nobody performed -- and the second is the checker-that-cannot-fail
defect wearing a paper trail. A STALE review is refused wherever it is
found, because that is a claim someone made.

natural-avg-pair.finding: Re-reviewed for draw 15 against env=2629, not inherited. The sweep is unchanged from the ADR-1115 review ([['avg', 'Nat.avg', 1]]) and the one declaration it names is Nat.avg itself, ADR-1060's Definition (Nat.avg a b := div (add a b) 2). Two mechanical checks with a working positive control (shape_search --const Nat.countRange is FOUND 21): --const Nat.avg is ABSENT and --const Nat.pair is ABSENT, so no declaration in this kernel has either constant anywhere in its type. The ten drawn rows (Nat.add_le_pair, Nat.avg_comm, Nat.avg_le_left, Nat.avg_le_right, Nat.avg_lt_left, Nat.avg_lt_right, Nat.le_add_one_of_avg_eq_left, Nat.le_add_one_of_avg_eq_right, Nat.le_avg_left, Nat.le_avg_right) were each compared against it: nine are order facts about Nat.avg and one is m + n <= Nat.pair m n, and none is settled here under any name. THE PAIR SIDE, which the stem sweep does not cover because Nat.pair is a subject of only 1 of 10 rows, below SUBJECT_FRACTION: 16 environment declarations contain `pair`, and the count and the reading both still hold at env=2629 -- Nat.pair is ADR-1060's Cantor-style pairing (Definition, no theorem); Nat.Pair/.mk/.fst/.snd/.fst_mk/.snd_mk/.ext/.eta/.rec are the inductive PAIR TYPE from binary_rec.rs, a different object whose Rust field is named pair_fn precisely to keep them apart; Nat.restrict_pair_injective and Nat.restrict_pair_maps_into are compact_pair/expand_pair index reindexing from the Gauss-lemma work; Int.prod_range_pairing_collapse, CPoint.cevian_pair_meet, CReal.geom_pair_within and Rat.PairwiseUncorrelated are unrelated mathematics sharing a word. Nothing states m + n <= Nat.pair m n. WHAT THIS REVIEW ADDS OVER ADR-1115's, which is why it was redone rather than carried: ADR-1160 measured that R12's clean report is necessary and not sufficient, because a forall-quantified DEFINING EQUATION is settled by reduction and invisible to a binder-free classifier. Applying that reading here, which the earlier review predates: none of the ten is a boundary equation of Nat.avg or Nat.pair -- there is no avg 0 b, no avg a a, no pair 0 b in the drawn ten, and the nearest candidate, Nat.avg_comm : a.avg b = b.avg a, is NOT refl, because Nat.add recurses on its right argument so div (add a b) 2 and div (add b a) 2 are not definitionally equal at symbolic a and b; it needs Nat.add_comm under the division. This row stays live: if any declaration matching `avg` lands, the sweep changes and R11 refuses it as stale rather than passing it.

The "size" stem's 6 hits are 5 genuine Nat.size declarations (Nat.size, Nat.sizeAux, Nat.size_zero, Nat.size_aux_lt_pow, Nat.lt_pow_size) plus one false positive (CReal.meshLevelCount_ge_of_size, an unrelated CReal integration-mesh construction). Compared against the drawn ten (Nat.bit_add, Nat.bit_add', Nat.bit_false_zero, Nat.bit_le, Nat.bit_lt_bit, Nat.bit_ne_zero, Nat.size_bit, Nat.size_eq_zero, Nat.size_le_size, Nat.size_one): none is a mirror by name, and Mathlib's Nat.bit : Bool -> Nat -> Nat matches our kernel's own Nat.bit signature exactly, so this is a genuine subject-level overlap (this kernel could plausibly prove several of these rows from existing infrastructure) -- the same judgment call ADR-0900 recorded and left unresolved ("a judgement call, and it does not by itself solve this draw"), and the same shape as the accepted natural-square-root precedent (Nat.sqrt/sqrt_zero/sqrt_one already declared, none a literal mirror of the held-out rows). natural-find-greatest.finding: Live sweep reproduced in this worktree against a FRESHLY REBUILT shape_search (env=2629, four declarations more than ADR-1160's 2625 -- Int.pow_neg_one_of_even/_odd, Int.secondSupplementaryLaw, Nat.half_ceil_parity, none of them touching this family). The four stems resolve to 24 declarations and every one was read by name against the ten drawn statements (Nat.findGreatest_eq, _eq_iff, _eq_zero_iff, _is_greatest, _le, _mono, _mono_left, _mono_right, _of_ne_zero, _of_not). NOTHING SETTLES ANY OF THEM, and two independent mechanical checks say so rather than a count: the environment dump contains the string `findGreatest` exactly ONCE and it is the Definition, and `shape_search --const Nat.findGreatest` is ABSENT -- run with a working positive control, which matters here because the FIRST control I used (`--concl Nat.countRange`) also returned ABSENT: `--concl` indexes the conclusion HEAD, which for an equation is `Eq`, so three earlier ABSENT verdicts of mine proved nothing. `--const Nat.countRange` is FOUND 21 and is the control the verdicts above are read against. `find_greatest.rs` carries one Declaration::Definition and zero `.theorem(` call sites, checked in the source rather than inherited from ADR-1160. STEM BY STEM. `decidable` (20) is the logic prelude's decidability plumbing -- Decidable, .and/.byCases/.decide/.decide_eq_true_iff/.em/.isFalse/.isTrue/.not/.ofBool/.of_decide_eq_false/.of_decide_eq_true/.or/.rec, DecidablePred -- plus Rat.decidable_le and three string-prelude equality deciders, all unrelated, and Nat.lnp_decidable, which is the one that needed real reading (below). `greatest` (2) is Int.gcd_greatest, the gcd characterization, an unrelated function sharing a word -- the same false-positive class natural-square-root's accepted review names -- and Nat.findGreatest itself. `decidablepred` (1) and `find` (1) are the two new constructions. THE AWKWARD FINDING, which the stem sweep reaches only by accident and which no gate flags: this kernel has a LEAST-number principle over decidable predicates, and one form of it is BOUNDED. Nat.lnp_bounded_search : forall (Q : Nat -> Prop), (forall n, Or (Q n) (Not (Q n))) -> forall n, Or (forall k, Lt k n -> Not (Q k)) (exists m, And (Lt m n) (And (Q m) (forall k, Lt k m -> Not (Q k)))) -- a bounded search over a pointwise-decided predicate WITH the extremality clause, which is the structural dual of what findGreatest_eq_iff and findGreatest_eq_zero_iff characterize. Its siblings are Nat.lnp_decidable (the Bool-valued form), Nat.lnp_of_pointwise_decision, Nat.lnp_unrestricted_implies_em and Nat.em_implies_lnp. NONE of them states any drawn row: they are about the LEAST element, they are free-standing existence disjunctions rather than characterizations of a defined function, and not one mentions Nat.findGreatest (which cannot occur in any of them -- it was declared yesterday and the --const query above is ABSENT). But a producer arriving at findGreatest_eq_zero_iff has lnp_bounded_search's induction-on-the-bound skeleton available and can transport it, so this family is materially less blind than a sweep of ['decidable', 'greatest', 'decidablepred', 'find'] suggests, and a held-out result here should be read knowing that. Recorded as a disclosure and not a refusal on ADR-0654's stated rule: a blind family must be allowed to use developed tools or nothing could ever be held out. FOUR MORE THINGS THE STEM SWEEP CANNOT REACH, enumerated by hand against the dump because a name-based screen is blind to a proof under a different name (the Mathlib.Data.Nat.Count failure this whole review exists because of). (1) Nat.exists_most_significant_bit : forall n, Not (Eq n zero) -> exists i, And (Eq (testBit n i) one) (forall j, Lt i j -> Eq (testBit n j) zero) is the nearest thing in the environment to findGreatest_is_greatest's CONTENT -- a greatest satisfying index, with everything above it failing. It is unbounded above, specific to testBit, and an existence statement rather than a function characterization, so it settles nothing here; its fuel-induction route (Nat.msb_exists_of_le_fuel) is another transportable skeleton and is disclosed for the same reason as the LNP family. (2) Nat.sqrt and Nat.nthRoot are bounded greatest-satisfying searches at specific predicates; Nat.sqrt carries only sqrt_zero/sqrt_one/no_rational_sqrt_two and Nat.nthRoot/nthRootAux carry no theorem at all, so none proves any of the ten. (3) Nat.nth/nthAux select the n-th ASCENDING witness, not the greatest below a bound, and likewise carry no theorem. (4) Nat.countRange and its 25 lemmas count witnesses; every one concludes about countRange and none about a greatest witness. Also read and cleared: Nat.least_divisor_search, Nat.leastResidue and Nat.least_residue_* (least-divisor / least-residue searches, unrelated predicates). REDUCTION CHECK, because ADR-1115's classifier is necessary and not sufficient. R12 reports 0 of 10 and that is true but weak: is_closed_evaluation is binder-free by construction, so a forall-quantified DEFINING EQUATION is invisible to it. Reading the ten instead: none is a boundary equation of Nat.findGreatest. The nearest is findGreatest_of_not : Not (P (n+1)) -> findGreatest P (n+1) = findGreatest P n, which is the else-branch of the recursion gated on a hypothesis -- NOT refl, because our construction branches through Decidable.byCases on `dp (succ m)`, a variable applied to a term, which never iota-reduces at a symbolic argument; the row needs the negative elimination supplied explicitly. The two rows that WOULD be refl, Nat.findGreatest_succ and Nat.findGreatest_zero, are pool rows 12 and 13 and fall outside the drawn ten by the alphabet alone (pool 15, drawn 0..9, re-measured here with select()'s own screen). No module was added or removed to put them there. A layout combining Mathlib.Data.Nat.Find with any other module changes which ten are drawn and must re-run this screen; draw 15 takes the module alone.

natural-nth-root.finding: REDONE for ADR-1245 against env=2708, not amended: the previous review described env=2629 and its recorded sweep ([['root','CReal.ivt_exact_root',11],...]) no longer matched the live one, because Nat.ceilRoot and Nat.floorRoot (ADR-1245, this lane) took the stem 'root' from 11 declarations to 13. ALL 13 READ BY NAME: CReal.ivt_exact_root, CReal.ivt_exact_root_at, CReal.ivt_exact_root_decides_sign (bisection root-finding over CReal, an unrelated construction over a different carrier); Complex.I_is_fourth_root, Complex.IsRootOfUnity, Complex.geom_sum_eq_zero_of_root_of_unity, Complex.one_is_root_of_unity, Complex.root_of_unity_mul, Complex.root_of_unity_pow (roots of unity over Complex, unrelated mathematics sharing the word 'root'); Nat.nthRoot, Nat.nthRootAux (this draw's own ADR-0910 construction, necessarily self-matching); and the two NEW ones, Nat.ceilRoot and Nat.floorRoot. The 'nth' stem's four are Nat.nth and Nat.nthAux (draw 7's natural-nth-selector well-founded selector, a different function despite the shared stem) plus nthRoot/nthRootAux again; the 'nthroot' stem's two are nthRoot/nthRootAux. THE ONLY NEW QUESTION IS WHETHER THE TWO NEW DECLARATIONS SETTLE ANY DRAWN ROW, AND THEY DO NOT -- they are different functions, measured rather than argued. Nat.nthRoot n a is the greatest m with m^n <= a (an ORDER statement); Nat.floorRoot n a is the greatest b with b^n | a and Nat.ceilRoot n a the least b >= 1 with a | b^n (DIVISIBILITY statements, the adjoints of b |-> b^n on the divisor lattice). They disagree at small arguments and the committed test suite pins the disagreement: factorization_root_tests::the_two_roots_disagree_with_each_other_and_with_the_numeric_root asserts floorRoot 2 12 = 2, ceilRoot 2 12 = 6 AND nthRoot 2 12 = 3, the last so the disagreement cannot be vacuous through a broken nthRoot. The boundary conventions differ too: nthRoot 0 a = 1 while ceilRoot 0 a = floorRoot 0 a = 0. Substituting floorRoot into a drawn row makes it FALSE, not merely unproved: Nat.le_nthRoot_iff reads a <= n.nthRoot b <-> a^n <= b, and at (n,a,b) = (2,3,12) the floorRoot form is 3 <= 2 (false) <-> 9 <= 12 (true). MECHANICAL CHECKS, each with a working positive control (shape_search --include-constructed --const Nat.countRange is FOUND 21 at declarations=2708): --const Nat.nthRoot is ABSENT, so no declaration in this kernel mentions Nat.nthRoot anywhere in its type and the kernel has still never proved a theorem ABOUT it -- the same finding as the previous review, re-derived at the new environment rather than inherited. --const Nat.ceilRoot and --const Nat.floorRoot are ABSENT as well, which is ADR-0653's construction-only promise measured rather than asserted. The ten drawn rows are UNCHANGED by these declarations: ADR-1245's screen ran the frozen-family drawn-ten churn check and 0 of 42 families churn, so no row was added, removed or reordered. R11's topic, vocabulary and environment-threshold signals are all clean; the stale review was the single refusal reason and this row is what clears it. TWO THINGS RECORDED BECAUSE THEY ARE AWKWARD, NEITHER OF WHICH REFUSES THE FAMILY. (1) The stem sweep is a NAME sweep: ceilRoot/floorRoot matched it only because they contain the letters 'root', and it could not have told a divisibility root from an order root either way -- had this lane named them Nat.divisorFloor the sweep would not have moved at all, and the genuine adjacency question would have been exactly as live. The count is a trigger for reading, never evidence on its own. (2) A SHAPE adjacency does exist and should be watched: Nat.pow_dvd_iff_dvd_floorRoot (a^n | b <-> a | n.floorRoot b) is the divisibility adjunction, and the held-out Nat.le_nthRoot_iff (a <= n.nthRoot b <-> a^n <= b) is the order adjunction, so their PROOF SKELETONS would rhyme. Nothing of the sort exists today (both --const probes ABSENT), and R11 asks whether a drawn row is settled, which it is not. But the lane that lands factorization_root's supporting theorems from development should re-run this screen first: that is the documented shape-2 blindness, and it would arrive through a legitimate development proof rather than through anything a name comparison sees.

refused.finding: Reviewed for draw 14 and REFUSED, so this is deliberately not a `reviews` row: a review row is a licence to draw. R11's three signals are clean and that is not the problem -- topic 0, vocabulary 4 of 10 (allowance 5), and the stem sweep resolves benignly. The 99 hits on stem `prime` are dominated by `coprime`, which merely CONTAINS the substring: read by name, they are the Nat.coprime_* / Nat.prime_* / totient / gcd development, and none states any drawn row, all four of which conclude about Abundant/Deficient/Perfect. The stems `abundant`, `deficient` and `perfect` each resolve to exactly one declaration and it is the Definition itself, with no theorem about it. WHAT REFUSES IT IS R12, once its classifier can see the shape. Nat.abundant_twelve (`Nat.Abundant 12`) and Nat.deficient_one (`Nat.Deficient 1`) are ground predicate applications over constants this kernel declares, decided by reduction with no mathematical content. Measured, not argued: nat_prelude/abundant_deficient_tests.rs already asserts def_eq(Nat.Abundant 12, Lt 24 28). R12 could not classify them because `is_closed_evaluation` required an `=`; ADR-1115 extended it, and R12 now names both rows. Both sort into the alphabetically-first ten, and this generator has no lawful mechanism to drop one row from an alphabetically-drawn pool. TWO FURTHER FINDINGS a future reader needs, neither of which is a refusal on its own. (1) The stem sweep does NOT reach Nat.sumDivisors, because `sumdivisors` is not a stem of Abundant/Deficient/Perfect/Prime -- yet all three predicates are DEFINED through it. Enumerated by hand: Nat.sumDivisors plus four theorems (sumDivisors_one, sumDivisors_prime, sumDivisors_two_pow, sumDivisors_two_pow_eq_geom_sum). Nat.sumDivisors_prime (`Prime p -> sumDivisors p = succ p`) makes Nat.Prime.deficient, Nat.Prime.not_abundant and Nat.Prime.not_perfect cheap rather than open -- each becomes an order fact about p + 1 against 2p, with Nat.prime_one_lt already present. Nothing PROVES them, so the rows are blind in the letter; a reader deciding what a held-out result here would mean needs to know they are much easier than the module name suggests. (2) Nat.Perfect is already declared and our Nat.Abundant / Nat.Deficient are stated against the SAME Nat.sumDivisors, so the family's trichotomy rows (abundant_iff_not_perfect_and_not_deficient and its sibling) are an arithmetic trichotomy on sumDivisors n against 2n rather than a factorisation argument.
